findings.source: Cellar.sol uint32[] public creditPositions / debtPositions; e.g. :1004 uint32 position = creditPositions[i]; getPositionData[position]; swapPositions: (creditPositions[index1], creditPositions[index2]) = (creditPositions[index2], creditPositions[index1]);
findings.issue: def storage knows stor10/stor11 are arrays (it prints stor10.length), but element reads and writes of these packed uint32 arrays (8 elements per slot) stay raw slot arithmetic with shifts by 32 * (i % 8), repeated up to 10 times per loop iteration as the key of getPositionData.
findings.rule: For element width w = 256 / k bits: Mask(w, w * (i % k), stor[i / k + sha3(s)]) >> w * (i % k) is element i of the array at slot s, and 'stor[i / k + sha3(s)] = (v << w*(i % k)) | ~(M << w*(i % k)) & stor[..]' is the write stor_s[i] = v; print stor10[idx] (and bind it once).

findings.source: Cellar.sol getCreditPositions() returns (uint32[] memory) { return creditPositions; }
findings.issue: The compiler's storage-to-memory copy of a packed uint32[] is printed as a twice-rotated loop over a byte offset and a slot counter (s = (s + 4) % 32, t += (s == 28)); a one-line function becomes 25 lines, followed by a second re-encoding loop.
findings.rule: A loop writing mem[d + 32k] = uint_w(stor[base + k / (256/w)] >> w * (k % (256/w))) for k < len (offset update s' = (s + w/8) % 32, slot update t' = t + (s + w/8 == 32)) is the copy 'mem[d len 32 * len] = stor10[0 len len]'; fold the peeled first iterations back into it.
findings.verified: reading only (checked the offset update: for s in {0,4,..,24} it gives s + 4, for s = 28 it gives 0 and t + 1)

findings.rule: 'while s < n: mem[a + s] = stor[b + s/32]; s += 32' is the copy 'mem[a len ceil32(n)] = stor[b len ceil32(n)]'; print it as a copy line like the other copies.

findings.source: Cellar.sol callOnAdaptor: minimumAllowedAssets = assetsBeforeAdaptorCall.mulDivUp((1e18 - allowedRebalanceDeviation), 1e18); maximumAllowedAssets = ...mulDivUp((1e18 + allowedRebalanceDeviation), 1e18)
findings.issue: Solmate mulDivUp is printed with x * (1e18 +/- d) distributed (P9) and its rounding as '(p - 1) / d * bool(p) + bool(p)', with the product written three times.
findings.rule: Keep a * (b + c) undistributed when b + c is an operand of the source; '(p - 1) / d * bool(p) + bool(p)' with p = x*y is ceil(p / d) (mulDivUp); bind p once.

notes: Small functions (ERC20/ERC4626 views, owner setters, catalogue add/remove, multicall, swapPositions, getCreditPositions/getDebtPositions, executeOperation's prologue) reviewed in detail; totalAssets/totalAssetsWithdrawable, maxRedeem/maxWithdraw, deposit/mint/redeem/withdraw, multiAssetDeposit, callOnAdaptor, cachePriceRouter, addPosition/removePosition/forcePositionOut reviewed by structure. Loops: 10 source loops compiled here, all whiles: multicall's for ('while True: if s >= data.length: stop', 916), executeOperation's for (2734), _calculateTotalAssetsOrTotalAssetsWithdrawable's 3 fors (credit-withdrawable 1868, credit 3000, debt 3082 and their copies in cachePriceRouter, callOnAdaptor, maxRedeem, maxWithdraw), _makeAdaptorCalls' nested fors (4922 / 4939), _withdrawInOrder (3325, 3678), Uint32Array.add (2320, 2348) and remove (1598 ... 1798). Not counted: PriceRouter._getValues (:594), listed in the pack's reach but reached only through the external call priceRouter.getValues / getValuesDelta. The other whiles are implicit: 30 memory-to-memory copies left as loops (P7: bytes arguments of delegatecalls, the 'Address: low-level delegate call failed' message, ABI encodings of uint256[] for the price router), 19 storage-bytes-to-memory copies (finding 3), 2 packed-array copies with 2 peeled iterations each (P3, finding 2), address re-encodings 'Bytes(12, 0), mem[s + 12 len 20]', 2 calldata decodes of AdaptorCall[] / bytes[]. P11: receive is 'require calldata.size < 4; require not calldata.size'; ~40 Panic(50) checks implied by the loop bound (e.g. 'if idx >= mem[_10]' where mem[_10] = stor10.length, the inner loop's repeated 'if s >= mem[..]'). In callOnAdaptor the same length is read as mem[_155 + ceil32(return_data.size)] before the loop and mem[_155 + ceil32(_1)] inside it (equal values, as no call intervenes before the loop). The storage struct getPositionData (stor13) shows its bytes members as field_256/field_257/field_264 with the short/long string decoding inline.
summary: Faithful, and all ten compiled source loops are whiles, but the packed uint32 position arrays are never recognized (437 lines of slot/shift arithmetic, an unreadable rotated copy loop in getCreditPositions), and storage-bytes and memory copies are left as loops.
